title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 117
paragraphs: Such was the reward they received. As for the Persians, passing on from Thrace they came to the crossing, where they crossed the Hellespont in haste to Abydos by means of the ships — for they did not find the floating bridges still stretched across, but broken up by a storm. While staying there for a time they were given more abundant rations than they had received on the way, and from sating their hunger without restraint and from the changes of water, many of those in the army who had survived until then died. The rest arrived with Xerxes at Sardis.
